transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks, especially on video calls and in salsa photos. Everyone tells me they don’t see it, but I do, and it’s starting to affect my work and my social life.
Do you think it’s possible that other people are right and the problem with your face is not really noticeable, or are you certain that it is definitely there?

I mean, everyone keeps telling me they don’t notice it, so maybe it isn’t as obvious to them. But I can’t stop seeing how uneven and puffy the left side looks, especially on video calls or in salsa photos. It feels very noticeable to me, and it’s been messing with work and seeing people.
Because of your concern about your face, do you find yourself repeatedly checking it in mirrors or on camera?

Yes. Before meetings or before I go out, I’ll keep opening the camera preview and changing the angle or lighting. I fix my hair to cover that side, retake pictures, and ask friends if I look strange. Sometimes I do it so long that I’m late, or I get too drained and don’t want to go.
Do you avoid seeing people because you’re afraid they’ll judge or notice something wrong with your face?

Yes. I’ve skipped salsa nights and community events when I knew people would be taking photos. And with work, I’ve joined video calls late or missed ticket deadlines because I couldn’t get past how I looked beforehand. My supervisor even mentioned it in my performance review.
When you avoid video calls, photos, or going out, is it mainly because you’re afraid other people will notice and judge that part of your face?

Yes. I’m worried people will notice it and judge me, especially if there are photos or video. I’ve skipped salsa nights and community events for that reason, and at work I’ve joined calls late or missed ticket deadlines because I couldn’t get past how I looked. My supervisor even brought it up in my performance review.
Are you ever completely convinced that your face is definitely deformed, even when other people tell you it looks normal?
Sometimes, yes. On video especially, the left side looks so uneven and puffy to me that I feel sure something is wrong with it, even when people tell me they don’t see it.
Outside of worries about your face, do you generally fear being judged or embarrassed in social situations?
I’m not sure. It’s mostly tied to my face—feeling like people will notice that and think something is wrong.
Do you get unwanted thoughts about your face that keep coming into your mind even when you try to resist them?

Yes. It keeps coming back, especially before video calls or when I see photos from salsa. I try to tell myself other people don’t notice it, but I keep focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side looks.
Is your worry mainly about how your face looks, rather than about other kinds of social embarrassment or judgment?

Yes, mainly my face. I keep fixating on how uneven and puffy the left side looks on video calls and in photos from salsa. People tell me they don’t see it, but I can’t stop thinking about it, and it’s starting to affect work and seeing people.
Do you spend a lot of time comparing the left side of your face with the right side?

Yes. Before meetings or going out, I keep checking the camera preview and changing the angle or lighting to compare both sides. I’ll fix my hair around that side, retake pictures, and ask friends if I look strange. Sometimes I end up late or too drained to go.
Do these thoughts and urges to check mainly happen because of how your face looks, rather than because of other upsetting thoughts or rituals?

Yes. It’s because of how that side of my face looks. Before meetings or going out, I’ll keep opening the camera preview, changing the angle and lighting, fixing my hair, retaking pictures, and asking friends if I look strange. I can get stuck doing it until I’m late or just too drained to go.
Have you been preoccupied with any other parts of your appearance besides the left side of your face?
No, it’s really the left side of my face. I keep noticing how uneven and puffy it looks on video calls or in photos from salsa, even though other people say they don’t see it.
Right now, do you believe the left side of your face truly looks abnormal to other people?

Yes, I do. On video calls and in photos from salsa, the left side looks noticeably uneven and puffy to me. I know people keep saying they don’t see it, but I still feel like it must be obvious to them.
Have you seen a doctor or cosmetic specialist about the left side of your face?
I haven’t seen a doctor or cosmetic specialist about it. I’ve thought about it, but I haven’t made an appointment.
Are you mainly worried that your face looks unattractive or abnormal, rather than that the puffiness means there is a medical problem?

Yes. I’m mainly worried about how it looks—that the left side of my face seems uneven and puffy, especially on video calls or in salsa photos. I can’t stop focusing on it, even when people tell me they don’t notice anything, and it’s starting to affect my work and social life.
